title: Turn flow: question, retrieval, agent loop, tools
description: A turn, by the question you are asking of it. Reading one turn is a log, so the narrative is first. How turns behave is a metric. Why one was slow is a trace, which is the only question a waterfall answers better than a log line. Spans carry structure and timing and no text: Tempo truncates an attribute at 2048 bytes, so content rides a log record instead, written only on a developer stack and dropped by the collector unless it holds its own key too (ADR-0025).

panels.title: Every turn, as a log
panels.description: One record per turn: the question, the scope decision and the rule that made it, retrieval and the evidence it chose, the seeds, then each round with the tool it ran, and how the turn ended. This is the readable account; the trace panels below are for when the question is timing. Developer stack only, behind three keys (ADR-0025): the application writes the record when TELEMETRY_DEBUG_CONTENT=1 and APP_ENV is local or test, and the collector drops it unless its own OTEL_ALLOW_CONTENT_LOGS=1. On a deployed stack this panel is empty, and that is correct rather than broken.

panels.title: The request, the answer, and what the gate withheld
panels.description: app_content_kind: "messages" is the literal array the model was sent, whole, which a span attribute cannot hold because Tempo truncates one at 2048 bytes; "answer" is what was released; "withheld" is what the evidence gate held back and appears in no other record, since the request array is what the model was sent rather than what it produced. Developer stack only, behind three keys (ADR-0025): the application writes the record when TELEMETRY_DEBUG_CONTENT=1 and APP_ENV is local or test, and the collector drops it unless its own OTEL_ALLOW_CONTENT_LOGS=1. On a deployed stack this panel is empty, and that is correct rather than broken.

panels.title: Why a turn was slow: traces
Turns: pick one to open its flow
panels.description: Spans carry the structure and timing of a turn and none of its text. Click the trace id for the waterfall, or the run handle for every log record of that turn.

targets.query: { name = "turn" } | select(span.app.turn.run_handle, span.app.turn.scope_label, span.app.turn.run_state, span.app.turn.reason, span.app.turn.citations, span.app.retrieval.seed_source, span.app.retrieval.items)

value.title: Turn log: this turn as a log, and the request it sent

panels.title: Agent rounds: what each round did and why it ended
panels.description: One row per pass through the loop. app.agent.round counts passes; app.agent.iterations counts only the rounds that ran tools, which is what the cap is measured against, so a capped turn shows two rounds at the same iteration count. stop_reason: tool_use, end_turn, iterations, deadline, aborted, model_error, output_blocked, or tool_budget_exhausted when a round was refused more tools.

targets.query: { name = "agent.round" } | select(span.app.agent.round, span.app.agent.iterations, span.app.agent.stop_reason, span.app.agent.tools_requested, span.app.error.code)

panels.title: Tool calls: name, status and the round they belong to
panels.description: status: ok, timeout, error, refused, unknown, or index for a pre-run the system ran before the model's first turn (round 0). Arguments and results are not here; they are in the request array above.

panels.title: Model calls: the provider leg of each round
panels.description: The outbound call to the gateway. Its duration against the round duration above separates model latency from tool latency, which is the one question a waterfall answers better than a log.

panels.title: Turns per minute, by scope and outcome
panels.description: app_turns_total, split by the scope the classifier assigned, the state the run ended in, and whether the evidence gate released the answer.

panels.title: Withheld by the evidence gate, by mechanism
panels.description: app_gate_withheld_total. A mechanism other than a quoted comment means a budget or the verifier removed the last piece of evidence for a sentence.

panels.title: Security events on the turn path
Catalogued events (click trace to open the flow)
panels.description: injection.suspected, answer.claim_withheld, policy.enforced, canary.followed, question.url_requested, content.url_masked, content.pii_masked, egress.forbidden, error.unhandled. Fields are catalogue-capped, so no request content rides here whatever the developer flag says.
